## Set the two common differences equal
In an arithmetic sequence $T_2 - T_1 = T_3 - T_2$.
(5p-3) - (2p+1) &= (6p+7) - (5p-3)
5p - 3 - 2p - 1 &= 6p + 7 - 5p + 3
3p - 4 &= p + 10
## Solve for p
2p - 4 &= 10
2p &= 14
p &= 7
ANSWER: p = 7

## (i) Differentiate F0 to get F1
Use $\frac{d}{dx}x^k = kx^{k-1}$.
F_1(x) &= 2024x^{2023}
## (i) Differentiate F1 to get F2
F_2(x) &= 2024 \times 2023\, x^{2022}
## (ii) Spot the pattern in the power
Each derivative lowers the power of $x$ by 1.
\text{power in } F_n &= 2024 - n
## (ii) Find when F_n becomes a constant
At $n = 2024$ the power is $0$, so $F_{2024}$ is a constant (it equals $2024!$ times $x^0$).
The derivative of a constant is $0$, so $F_{2025} = 0$.
Every earlier $F_n$ still contains a power of $x$ with a non-zero coefficient, so it is not $0$ for $x>0$.
ANSWER: n = 2025

## Use the factor theorem
If $x-4$ is a factor of $h(x)$ then $h(4)=0$.
h(4) &= 0
## Substitute x = 4 and solve for b
4^2 + 4b - 12 &= 0
16 + 4b - 12 &= 0
4b + 4 &= 0
4b &= -4
b &= -1
ANSWER: b = -1

## Substitute x = 1.2
f(1.2) &= e^{9(1.2)}
&= e^{10.8}
## Evaluate and write in the form a × 10^n
&= 49020.8\ldots
&= 4.9 \times 10^4
ANSWER: 4.9 \times 10^4

## Work out the tax at 20%
\text{Tax at 20\%} &= 0.2 \times 40000
&= 8000
## Find the amount taxed at 40%
\text{Remainder} &= 54000 - 40000
&= 14000
## Work out the tax at 40%
\text{Tax at 40\%} &= 0.4 \times 14000
&= 5600
## Add to get the gross tax
\text{Gross tax} &= 8000 + 5600
&= 13600
## Subtract the tax credit
The tax credit reduces the tax Fiadh has to pay.
\text{Tax payable} &= 13600 - 1775
&= 11825
## Subtract the tax from her salary
\text{Net pay} &= 54000 - 11825
&= 42175
ANSWER: \text{€}42\,175

## Write the monthly rate as a decimal
Each month the debt grows by a factor of $1 + 0.00279 = 1.00279$.
0.279\% &= 0.00279
## Present value of repayment 1
A payment made after $n$ months is divided by $1.00279$ once for each month.
PV_1 &= \frac{1647.75}{1.00279}
## Present value of repayment 2
PV_2 &= \frac{1647.75}{(1.00279)^2}
## Present value of repayment 3
PV_3 &= \frac{1647.75}{(1.00279)^3}
## Set up the amount borrowed as a sum
The loan equals the sum of the present values of all $25 \times 12 = 300$ repayments.
P &= \frac{1647.75}{1.00279} + \frac{1647.75}{(1.00279)^2} + \cdots + \frac{1647.75}{(1.00279)^{300}}
## Identify the geometric series
This is a geometric series with $n = 300$, first term $a$ and common ratio $r$.
a &= \frac{1647.75}{1.00279}
r &= \frac{1}{1.00279}
## Substitute into the geometric sum formula
$S_n = \dfrac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}$
P &= \frac{\frac{1647.75}{1.00279}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{1.00279}\right)^{300}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{1.00279}}
## Evaluate and round
P &= 334\,562.61\ldots
P &\approx 334\,563
ANSWER: \text{€}334\,563

## Write the average value as an integral
Average value over $[0, 5]$ is $\dfrac{1}{5-0}\int_0^5 F(t)\,dt$.
\text{Average} &= \frac{1}{5}\int_0^5 5000 e^{0.04t}\,dt
## Integrate
Use $\int e^{kt}\,dt = \dfrac{e^{kt}}{k}$.
&= \frac{1}{5}(5000)\left[\frac{e^{0.04t}}{0.04}\right]_0^5
&= 1000\left[\frac{e^{0.04t}}{0.04}\right]_0^5
## Substitute the limits
&= 1000\left(\frac{e^{0.04(5)}}{0.04} - \frac{e^{0.04(0)}}{0.04}\right)
&= 1000\left(\frac{e^{0.2}}{0.04} - \frac{1}{0.04}\right)
&= 25000\left(e^{0.2} - 1\right)
## Evaluate and round
&= 5535.07\ldots
&\approx 5535
ANSWER: \text{€}5535

## Find the yearly growth factor
Over one year, $t$ increases by 1, so the account is multiplied by $e^{0.04}$.
\frac{F(1)}{F(0)} &= \frac{5000e^{0.04}}{5000e^{0}}
&= e^{0.04}
&= 1.04081\ldots
## Convert the increase to a percentage
\text{AER} &= (1.04081 - 1) \times 100
&\approx 4.08\%
ANSWER: 4.08\%

## Substitute x = 0
Replace $x$ by each value, work out the bracket, cube it, then add 70.
T(0) &= \left(\frac{0-240}{60}\right)^3 + 70
&= (-4)^3 + 70
&= -64 + 70 = 6
## Substitute x = 120
T(120) &= \left(\frac{120-240}{60}\right)^3 + 70
&= (-2)^3 + 70
&= -8 + 70 = 62
## Substitute x = 180
T(180) &= \left(\frac{180-240}{60}\right)^3 + 70
&= (-1)^3 + 70
&= -1 + 70 = 69
## Substitute x = 240
T(240) &= \left(\frac{240-240}{60}\right)^3 + 70
&= 0^3 + 70 = 70
## Substitute x = 300
T(300) &= \left(\frac{300-240}{60}\right)^3 + 70
&= 1^3 + 70 = 71
## Complete the table
The table is $x$: 0, 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360 and $T(x)$: 6, 43, 62, 69, 70, 71, 78.
## Plot the points and join them
Plot the seven points $(x, T(x))$. Join them with a smooth curve, not straight line segments.
ANSWER: 6,\ 43,\ 62,\ 69,\ 70,\ 71,\ 78

## Use the range of cosine
$\cos A$ is always between $-1$ and $1$.
S_{\max} &= 21 + 19(1)
&= 40
## Find the minimum
S_{\min} &= 21 + 19(-1)
&= 2
ANSWER: \text{Maximum} = 40,\ \text{Minimum} = 2

## Set the two functions equal
C(t) &= S(t)
S(t) - 2.4 + 0.03t &= S(t)
## Cancel S(t) from both sides
-2.4 + 0.03t &= 0
## Solve for t
0.03t &= 2.4
t &= \frac{2.4}{0.03}
t &= 80
ANSWER: t = 80 \text{ days}

## Look at the two parts of C(t)
$C(t) = S(t) - 2.4 + 0.03t$. $S(t)$ is a cosine wave, so it repeats up and down.
$-2.4 + 0.03t$ is a straight line with a positive slope $0.03$, so it increases steadily over time.
## Compare with the graphs
Graph J is a straight line only, so it has no wave. Graph K is a wave with no overall rise. Graph L is a wave that rises over time.
Adding the rising line to the wave makes the wave drift upwards, so the graph is L.
ANSWER: \text{Graph L}

## Set C'(t) = 0
Use radians on the calculator.
0.03 - \frac{38\pi}{365}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{365}\right) &= 0
## Isolate the sine term
\frac{38\pi}{365}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{365}\right) &= 0.03
\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{365}\right) &= \frac{0.03(365)}{38\pi}
\sin\left(\frac{2\pi t}{365}\right) &= 0.09172\ldots
## Take the inverse sine
The first time $C'(t)=0$ uses the smallest positive angle.
\frac{2\pi t}{365} &= \sin^{-1}(0.09172\ldots)
\frac{2\pi t}{365} &= 0.09185\ldots
## Solve for t
t &= \frac{0.09185(365)}{2\pi}
t &= 5.336\ldots
t &\approx 5
ANSWER: t = 5 \text{ days}

## Write down the formula
C &= \frac{\pi k^2}{3}(3R - k)
## Substitute R = 13 and k = 4
C &= \frac{\pi (4)^2}{3}\left(3(13) - 4\right)
## Simplify the brackets
C &= \frac{16\pi}{3}(39 - 4)
C &= \frac{16\pi}{3}(35)
## Multiply
C &= \frac{560\pi}{3}
ANSWER: C = \frac{560\pi}{3}

## Put R = 8 and k = y into the cap formula
C &= \frac{\pi y^2}{3}\left(3(8) - y\right)
C &= \frac{\pi y^2}{3}(24 - y)
## Set the volume equal to 36πy
\frac{\pi y^2}{3}(24 - y) &= 36\pi y
## Divide both sides by π
\frac{y^2}{3}(24 - y) &= 36y
## Divide both sides by y
This is allowed because $y > 0$.
\frac{y}{3}(24 - y) &= 36
## Multiply both sides by 3
y(24 - y) &= 108
## Multiply out the bracket
24y - y^2 &= 108
## Rearrange into a quadratic equal to zero
y^2 - 24y + 108 &= 0
## Factorise
Two numbers that multiply to $108$ and add to $-24$ are $-6$ and $-18$.
(y - 6)(y - 18) &= 0
## Solve for y
y &= 6 \text{ or } y = 18
## Reject the value that is too large
The sphere has radius $8$, so the height must satisfy $y \le 8$. Reject $y = 18$.
ANSWER: y = 6

## Convert litres to cm³
$1$ litre $= 1000\ \text{cm}^3$.
3 \text{ litres} &= 3000 \text{ cm}^3
## Set up the equation
\frac{\pi}{12}x^3 &= 3000
## Multiply both sides by 12
\pi x^3 &= 36000
## Divide both sides by π
x^3 &= \frac{36000}{\pi}
## Take the cube root
x &= \sqrt[3]{\frac{36000}{\pi}}
x &= 22.545\ldots
## Round to 1 decimal place
x &\approx 22.5
ANSWER: x = 22.5 \text{ cm}

## Write down what is given
The volume increases at $450\ \text{cm}^3$ per second.
\frac{dV}{dt} &= 450
## Differentiate V with respect to x
V &= \frac{\pi}{12}x^3
\frac{dV}{dx} &= \frac{3\pi}{12}x^2
&= \frac{\pi}{4}x^2
## Turn it upside down
\frac{dx}{dV} &= \frac{4}{\pi x^2}
## Use the chain rule
We want $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$, so link it to the two rates above.
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \frac{dx}{dV} \times \frac{dV}{dt}
## Substitute the two rates
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \frac{4}{\pi x^2} \times 450
&= \frac{1800}{\pi x^2}
## Substitute x = 20
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \frac{1800}{\pi (20)^2}
&= \frac{1800}{400\pi}
&= 1.432\ldots
## Round to 1 decimal place
\frac{dx}{dt} &\approx 1.4
ANSWER: 1.4 \text{ cm per second}

## Substitute x = 15 into W(x)
W(15) &= 0.667(15) + 1.5(15)^2 - 0.025(15)^3
## Work out each term
W(15) &= 10.005 + 1.5(225) - 0.025(3375)
&= 10.005 + 337.5 - 84.375
&= 263.13
## Round to the nearest mm
The question asks for the nearest mm.
W(15) &\approx 263
ANSWER: 263\text{ mm}

## Differentiate each term of W(x)
Use the rule: the derivative of $ax^n$ is $anx^{n-1}$.
W(x) &= 0.667x + 1.5x^2 - 0.025x^3
W'(x) &= 0.667(1) + 1.5(2x) - 0.025(3x^2)
&= 0.667 + 3x - 0.075x^2
ANSWER: W'(x) = 0.667 + 3x - 0.075x^2

## Write the inequality for P'(x) > 24
1.1 + 2.73x - 0.078x^2 &> 24
## Rearrange so one side is zero
Subtract 24 from both sides.
-0.078x^2 + 2.73x - 22.9 &> 0
Multiply both sides by $-1$ and reverse the inequality sign.
0.078x^2 - 2.73x + 22.9 &< 0
## Find the roots with the quadratic formula
Solve $0.078x^2 - 2.73x + 22.9 = 0$ with $a = 0.078$, $b = -2.73$, $c = 22.9$.
x &= \frac{2.73 \pm \sqrt{(2.73)^2 - 4(0.078)(22.9)}}{2(0.078)}
&= \frac{2.73 \pm \sqrt{7.4529 - 7.1448}}{0.156}
&= \frac{2.73 \pm \sqrt{0.3081}}{0.156}
x &\approx 21.06 \text{ or } x \approx 13.94
## Choose the values between the roots
The graph of $0.078x^2 - 2.73x + 22.9$ opens upwards, so it is below zero between the roots.
13.94 &< x < 21.06
## Round each value to the nearest whole number
14 &\le x \le 21
ANSWER: 14 \le x \le 21

## Use the reflection in the y-axis
Reflecting in the $y$-axis replaces $x$ with $-x$, so $k(x) = s(-x)$.
k(x) &= s(-x)
&= 2(-x) - (-x)^2
## Simplify k(x)
k(x) &= -2x - x^2
&= -x^2 - 2x + 0
## Compare with k(x) = -x^2 + bx + c
-x^2 + bx + c &= -x^2 - 2x + 0
The coefficients of $x$ match, and the constant terms match.
b &= -2 \text{ and } c = 0
ANSWER: b = -2,\; c = 0

## Price for Option 1
Reduce by 10% means multiply by $0.9$. Then subtract $r$.
\text{Option 1} &= 0.9p - r
## Price for Option 2
Subtract $r$ first, then multiply by $0.9$.
\text{Option 2} &= 0.9(p - r)
&= 0.9p - 0.9r
## Compare the two prices
\text{Option 1} - \text{Option 2} &= (0.9p - r) - (0.9p - 0.9r)
&= -r + 0.9r
&= -0.1r
Since $r > 0$, the difference is negative, so Option 1 costs less for every $p$ and $r$. Tick Option 1.
ANSWER: \text{Option 1 is cheaper: } 0.9p - r < 0.9p - 0.9r

## Find a from the mode
The mode is the most common value. In the row for 3, the leaf 4 appears twice already (34, 34), as does 57.
For 34 to be the mode it must appear more often than 57, so the leaf $a$ must also be 4.
a &= 4
## Find b and c from the range
The smallest value is $20 + b$ (first row) and the largest is $60 + c$ (last row).
(60 + c) - (20 + b) &= 49
40 + c - b &= 49
c - b &= 9
$b$ and $c$ are single digits, so the difference 9 needs $c = 9$ and $b = 0$.
b &= 0 \text{ and } c = 9
## Find d from the median
There are 22 values, so the median is the mean of the 11th and 12th values.
The first 8 values are in rows 2 and 3, then 40, 41, then $40 + d$ is the 11th. The 12th is 45.
\frac{(40 + d) + 45}{2} &= 43.5
(40 + d) + 45 &= 87
85 + d &= 87
d &= 2
ANSWER: a = 4,\; b = 0,\; c = 9,\; d = 2

## Compare the two tests
Every student swam further in the re-test than in the initial test, so everyone improved.
The improvements were not equal: 22 m rose by 3 m, but 61 m rose by 289 m.
The points curve upwards, not along a straight line, so the stronger swimmers improved by much more than the weaker ones.
## Find r with the calculator
Enter the initial test distances as $x$ and the re-test distances as $y$ in statistics mode, then read the correlation coefficient.
r &= 0.91451\ldots
r &\approx 0.9145
ANSWER: \text{The better swimmers improved more;}\; r = 0.9145

## Set up the expected value
Expected winnings = sum of (prize × probability). The game is fair, so the expected winnings equal the €10 cost.
(0)(0.3) + (2)(0.4) + (x-10)(0.28) + (x)(0.02) &= 10
## Expand the brackets
0.8 + 0.28x - 2.8 + 0.02x &= 10
## Collect and solve
0.3x - 2 &= 10
0.3x &= 12
x &= 40
ANSWER: x = 40

## Use mutually exclusive events
Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together.
P(A \cap B) &= 0
## Use the addition rule
P(A \cup B) &= P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)
&= 0.1 + 0.4 - 0
&= 0.5
ANSWER: P(A \cap B) = 0,\; P(A \cup B) = 0.5

## Link the complement to the union
To make $(C \cup D)'$ as large as possible, make $P(C \cup D)$ as small as possible.
P(C \cup D) &= P(C) + P(D) - P(C \cap D)
&= 0.5 + 0.7 - P(C \cap D)
## Make the overlap as big as possible
$P(C \cap D)$ cannot be bigger than $P(C) = 0.5$. This happens when $C$ lies inside $D$.
P(C \cup D)_{\min} &= 1.2 - 0.5
&= 0.7
## Take the complement
P[(C \cup D)^{\prime}]_{\max} &= 1 - 0.7
&= 0.3
ANSWER: 0.3

## Use the meaning of independent
Independent events would mean that rain makes no difference to whether I wear a coat.
If it is raining I am more likely to wear a coat than if it is not, so the events are not independent.
ANSWER: \text{Rain makes a coat more likely, so } P(F \mid E) \ne P(F)

## Write the area formula for a parallelogram
Area $= ab\sin C$, where $a$ and $b$ are adjacent sides and $C$ is the angle between them.
## Substitute the sides and the angle between them
\text{Area} &= |AB|\,|BC|\sin|\angle ABC|
&= (10)(13)\sin 110^\circ
## Calculate and round to the nearest cm²
&= 130\sin 110^\circ
&= 122.16\ldots
&= 122\ \text{cm}^2
ANSWER: 122\ \text{cm}^2

## Find the reference angle
\cos(2X) &= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
2X &= \cos^{-1}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 30^\circ
## Find all values of 2X between 0° and 720°
$\cos$ is positive in the 1st and 4th quadrants. Since $0^\circ \le X \le 360^\circ$, we need $0^\circ \le 2X \le 720^\circ$, which is two full turns.
First turn: $2X = 30^\circ$ or $360^\circ - 30^\circ = 330^\circ$.
Second turn: add $360^\circ$ to each, giving $390^\circ$ and $690^\circ$.
2X &= 30^\circ,\ 330^\circ,\ 390^\circ,\ 690^\circ
## Divide each value by 2
X &= 15^\circ,\ 165^\circ,\ 195^\circ,\ 345^\circ
ANSWER: X = 15^\circ,\ 165^\circ,\ 195^\circ,\ 345^\circ

## Set up the sine rule
$|MK|$ is opposite $\angle KLM = 25^\circ$, and $|ML|$ is opposite $\theta = \angle LKM$.
\frac{\sin\theta}{|ML|} &= \frac{\sin|\angle KLM|}{|MK|}
\frac{\sin\theta}{45} &= \frac{\sin 25^\circ}{15\sqrt{3}}
## Solve for sin θ
\sin\theta &= \frac{45\sin 25^\circ}{15\sqrt{3}}
&= \frac{45(0.4226\ldots)}{15\sqrt{3}}
&= 0.73196\ldots
## Find both angles between 0° and 180°
Sine is positive in the 1st and 2nd quadrants, so there are two angles.
\theta &= \sin^{-1}(0.73196) = 47.05^\circ
\theta &= 180^\circ - 47.05^\circ = 132.95^\circ
## Round to the nearest degree
\theta &= 47^\circ \ \text{or}\ 133^\circ
ANSWER: \theta = 47^\circ \ \text{or} \ 133^\circ

## Recall what the centroid is
The centroid is the point where the three medians meet. A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, so two medians are enough.
## Find the midpoint of PQ
Set the compass to more than half of $|PQ|$. Draw an arc above and below $PQ$ from $P$, then the same arcs from $Q$.
Join the two points where the arcs cross. This line cuts $PQ$ at its midpoint $M_1$. (Or measure $|PQ|$ and mark half of it.)
## Find the midpoint of QR
Repeat the arcs from $Q$ and $R$ and join the crossing points. This cuts $QR$ at its midpoint $M_2$.
## Draw two medians and mark the centroid
Draw the line from $R$ to $M_1$ and the line from $P$ to $M_2$.
These medians cross at $G$, the centroid. A third median from $Q$ to the midpoint of $PR$ would pass through $G$ too.
ANSWER: \text{Centroid } G = \text{intersection of the medians}

## Add a construction line
Draw a line through $B$ parallel to $DF$.
Label $X$ where it meets $AD$, and $Y$ where it meets $CF$.
## Show the triangles XBA and YBC are congruent
$|AB| = |BC|$ ... given.
$|\angle XAB| = |\angle BCY|$ ... alternate angles ($AD \parallel CF$, transversal $AC$).
$|\angle XBA| = |\angle CBY|$ ... vertically opposite angles.
So $\triangle XBA \equiv \triangle YBC$ ... ASA.
## Deduce that XB equals BY
$|BX| = |BY|$ ... corresponding sides of congruent triangles.
## Use the parallelogram DEBX
$DEBX$ has $DE \parallel XB$ (since $XB \parallel DF$) and $DX \parallel EB$ (since $AD \parallel BE$).
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $DEBX$ is a parallelogram.
$|DE| = |BX|$ ... opposite sides of a parallelogram.
## Use the parallelogram EBYF in the same way
Similarly, $EBYF$ is a parallelogram, so $|EF| = |BY|$.
## Put the results together
$|DE| = |BX| = |BY| = |EF|$.
So $|DE| = |EF|$.
ANSWER: |DE| = |EF|
